pages.text:
Cash Acquisition at $47.50 Per Share, a ~58.1% Premium Over Previous Close: The Deep Dive into Salesforce's Acquisition of Braze [M&A Strategy Analysis Report]
At a time when investors are worried that AI will erode demand for software, why is Salesforce buying another software company at a high price? Moreover, the acquisition is an all-cash deal at $47.50 per share, a premium of approximately 58.1% over the previous day's closing price of $30.04. Completion is expected in fiscal year 2028, and Salesforce has also stated that it will not change its earnings outlook for fiscal year 2027. The urgency of the purchase, which includes a premium, and the disclosure stance of not showing an impact on earnings seem, at first glance, to be at odds.
The subject of this case is Salesforce's all-cash acquisition of Braze, which possesses a customer engagement platform (a mechanism for managing notifications and messages delivered to customers), for an enterprise value of approximately $5.66 billion, and whether it can incorporate customer touchpoints in the AI era into its own product layer.
This article presents the following three points for investors and M&A practitioners.
Organize the framework of the disclosed facts and separate confirmed information from estimates.
Verify the acquisition price and market expectations to show what is known and what is unknown.
Present which figures should be looked at for future investment and deal judgments.
In-depth financial analysis and future scenarios will be covered in the paid section.
1. Overview and Strategic Intent of the Deal
Salesforce (NYSE: CRM) announced on October 20, 2026, that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Braze (NASDAQ: BRZE). [Confirmed]
The enterprise value is approximately $5.66 billion. Enterprise value is a measure of the 'total price of the company,' calculated by adding and subtracting interest-bearing debt and other items from the market capitalization of the stock. [Confirmed]
Holders of Braze's Class A common stock will receive $47.50 per share in cash. [Confirmed]
Completion is expected in fiscal year 2028. Conditions include a vote by Braze shareholders, regulatory approval, and other customary conditions. [Confirmed]
The agreement lists as a risk factor the possibility of termination that would require the payment of a termination fee (money paid when a contract ends under certain circumstances). [Confirmed]
Financial advisors are J.P. Morgan Securities for Salesforce and Qatalyst Partners for Braze. [Confirmed]
Braze plans to file a preliminary proxy statement (Schedule 14A) and other materials with the SEC (U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission). [Confirmed]
While the transaction amount in the deal data is 'undisclosed,' the enterprise value and per-share price have been disclosed in a joint press release. No undisclosed information regarding the Braze acquisition amount can be found in the materials obtained for this report.
Buyer's Objective: Filling a Four-Layer Gap
According to the press release, Braze's real-time engagement capabilities and AI-driven decision-making features are expected to complement Salesforce's four layers (Data 360, Customer 360, Agentforce, and SIForce) upon completion. Within Customer 360, it is positioned to strengthen cross-channel personalization (delivering tailored content for each customer) in Marketing Cloud. [Confirmed]
There is no explanation in the acquired materials regarding what SIForce refers to. [Unknown]
Braze's assets are as follows:
It has a cloud-native design based on event streaming (a method of processing customer actions as a flow as they occur). [Estimated]
It features AI-driven optimization capabilities called "BrazeAI." [Estimated]
It has approximately 2,770 customers, including Canva, Instacart, Urban Outfitters, and Venmo. [Confirmed]
Reuters reports that this acquisition is the latest bet to accelerate the transition to AI, amid investor concerns that the rapid spread of AI is eroding demand for traditional software. [Estimated]
Seller's Circumstances: Little Public Information
The reasons why Braze agreed to the sale—that is, its standalone growth prospects, funding needs, and the history of deliberations by the board of directors—are not written in the acquired materials. [Unknown]
The confirmed facts are that Braze is also advised by Qatalyst Partners and that a shareholder vote by Braze is required for the transaction to close. [Confirmed]
Financial figures such as Braze's revenue, profit, and interest-bearing debt are not included in the acquisition materials. [Unknown]
Salesforce does not expect any changes to its fiscal year 2027 performance outlook (guidance) due to this transaction. It will not update its long-term financial targets either. [Confirmed]
The buyer's most recent performance shows revenue of $11.13 billion for the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 (February–April 2026), a 13% increase year-over-year. [Confirmed]
Revenue for the second quarter (May–July 2026) was $11.35 billion, an 11% increase year-over-year. Full-year revenue guidance has been raised to $46.1–$46.4 billion. [Confirmed]
The Japanese commentary article on the second-quarter earnings is titled "Stock Price Up 23% in One Day." [Estimated]
This raises three points of discussion.
What does the decision not to adjust guidance mean for a deal expected to take over a year to complete?
What is the significance of choosing an acquisition as a means during a period when revenue growth is slowing from 13% to 11%?
Where and how quickly will Blaze's functionality be integrated into the four layers?
These answers will be explored in the paid section from the perspectives of finance and competition.
The purchase price is $47.50 per share, in all cash. [Confirmed]
According to reports, the previous day's closing price was $30.04. [Estimated]
Dividing $47.50 by $30.04 results in approximately 1.581 times, and the premium (the markup over the market price) is approximately 58.1%, which is also consistent arithmetically. This is also consistent with the approximately 58.1% figure reported in the news. [Estimated]
The enterprise value of approximately $5.66 billion is reported as approximately 895 billion yen. This can be read as a value converted at approximately 158 yen to the dollar. [Estimated]
Salesforce's revenue for the fiscal year ending January 2026 is $41.525 billion. [Confirmed]
Dividing the enterprise value of $5.66 billion by this revenue results in approximately 13.6%, which is slightly over 10% of the buyer's annual revenue. [Confirmed]
This is also at the 12% level relative to the full-year revenue guidance of $46.1 billion to $46.4 billion for fiscal year 2027. [Confirmed]
While large for the buyer, it is not a scale that would shake the buyer's own revenue structure.
Multiples: Lack of Comparative Benchmarks
Blaze's revenue and EBITDA (earning power before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization) are not included in the acquired materials. Therefore, the acquisition multiples (EV/EBITDA, EV/Revenue), which indicate how many years of the business's earning power the acquisition price represents, cannot be calculated. [Unknown]
On the Nihon Keizai Shimbun's individual page for Blaze, 25.813x is listed as the EV/EBITDA in a single row. However, it is impossible to confirm which period this value refers to. This value cannot be equated with the acquisition multiple derived from the current acquisition price. [Unknown]
For reference, in general M&A commentary, the average EV/EBITDA multiple is considered to be 8–10x, the all-industry average is 6–8x, and the benchmark for the IT sector is 8–15x. However, these are primarily benchmarks for small and medium-sized Japanese companies and do not serve as a basis for applying them directly to US-listed software companies. [Estimated]
The distribution of premiums and multiples for similar software acquisition deals is not in the acquired materials. Therefore, it is impossible to conclude solely from the data whether 58.1% is high or standard. [Unknown]
Market Reaction on the Day of the Announcement
Blaze's stock price was $45.37 as of 9:45 AM NY time (up $15.33, or +51.03% from the previous day). [Estimate]
The difference from the $47.50 acquisition price is $2.13, leaving a gap of approximately 4.7% relative to the acquisition price. [Estimate]
Salesforce's stock price was reported to have fallen 3% following the announcement. As of the same 9:45 AM, it was $241.07 (-0.57%). [Estimate]
What is the approximately 58.1% premium paying for in Blaze? Is it current earnings, future growth, or synergies for Salesforce?
How does the approximately 4.7% gap between the acquisition price and the market price account for the time required until completion and the conditions for regulatory and shareholder approval?
How can we distinguish whether the buyer's stock price decline is an evaluation of an acquisition equivalent to approximately 13% of revenue, or an evaluation of anxiety surrounding AI?
These questions cannot be answered simply by lining up numbers. The key is which numbers you compare and how you read them.
In Salesforce's acquisition, the three facts—a 58.1% premium, an approximately 4.7% price gap, and unchanged guidance—each send different messages. In chapters 3–6 of the paid section, we will use these discrepancies as clues to address the following four points.
An assessment of how the Blaze acquisition will impact Salesforce's financials and growth
The power dynamics with competitors and the role Blaze will play within the four-layer structure
Future scenarios leading up to completion
Perspectives that investors and M&A practitioners can take away for their own deal assessments

Salesforce Strikes $5.66 Billion Deal to Acquire Braze
Salesforce has agreed to acquire customer engagement software provider Braze Inc. in a transaction valued at approximately $5.66 billion, expanding its presence in digital marketing technology as businesses increasingly turn to automation and artificial intelligence to connect with customers.
Under the agreement, holders of Braze Class A common stock will receive $47.50 per share in cash, according to Reuters, which reported the transaction Tuesday.
Salesforce shares declined 2.6% in premarket trading following the announcement, Reuters reported, suggesting an initially cautious response from investors to the multibillion-dollar acquisition.
The deal is expected to close during Salesforce’s fiscal year 2028, subject to regulatory clearance and approval from Braze shareholders.
Acquisition Expands Salesforce’s Marketing Capabilities
The proposed purchase would add Braze’s customer engagement technology to Salesforce’s existing portfolio of enterprise software products, potentially strengthening its ability to help businesses deliver personalized communications across digital channels.
Braze specializes in software that allows companies to interact with customers based on their behavior, including through mobile applications, websites, email and messaging services.
According to Salesforce’s announcement, the acquisition is intended to bring Braze’s real-time engagement capabilities together with Salesforce’s customer relationship management platform and artificial intelligence products.

Salesforce’s 2.6% premarket share decline, as reported by Reuters, came as investors evaluated the financial implications of the acquisition and its potential contribution to the company’s broader software business.
The $5.66 billion enterprise valuation represents a substantial investment in customer engagement technology. The proposed acquisition would give Salesforce access to Braze’s established platform and customer relationships while extending its marketing software capabilities.

I Ran the Numbers on Salesforce. Here’s Where I Think It Could Be in 2030
Salesforce is building an AI agent empire while its stock sits near multi-year lows, and the math behind a potential 184% gain by 2030 comes down to whether three very specific things happen in the next four years.
Published October 20, 2026, 7:15am ET · 3 min read
Price Targets desk. Editor: Vandita Jadeja.
© Noam Galai / Getty Images Entertainment via Getty Images
Salesforce (NYSE:CRM | CRM Price Prediction | CRM Price Prediction) runs the world’s largest CRM platform, and it is turning into an AI agent company. Agentforce ARR passed $1.5 billion in the August quarter, up more than 240% year over year.
Even so, shares are down 6.44% year to date at $246.11. The gap between business momentum and the share price is the whole story, so I ran the numbers on one question: can Salesforce reach $700 per share by 2030?
What’s Holding Salesforce Back Right Now
The market concerns that AI agents will hollow out seat-based software, but Salesforce has spent the year making the opposite case, and investors remain skeptical. Shares fell 4.96% over the past month, even after a 9.6% rise this week. Over five years, the stock is down 13.98%.
Doubts about earnings quality remain too. Q2 FY27 non-GAAP EPS of $5.90 included a $2.53 per share boost from strategic investment gains. Free cash flow growth is guided to just 4% to 5% this year, and management noted volatile license revenue. With a beta of 1.256, Salesforce moves harder than the market when sentiment turns.
Wall Street Is Too Cautious on Salesforce. Here’s My Case
The consensus target is $285.68, roughly 16.1% higher than the current price. Coverage includes 6 strong buys, 32 buys, 15 holds, 0 sells and 2 strong sells. Our model’s one-year base case is $347.14, meaning 47.6% upside with a high confidence level of 0.9. The scenarios run from $282.43 in the bear case to $386.92 in the bull case.
In my view, analysts are still stuck on to a rough 2026 for the stock and are underweighting what the business is doing. 69% of analysts are bullish, and earnings growth adds 0.03 to our projections. cRPO grew 14%, and net-new annual contract value growth was the strongest in four years. Bank of America argued this week that the AI pivot will drive shares higher.
Here’s What It Takes for Salesforce to Reach $700
Reaching $700 from today’s price of $246.11 would require a gain of 184.4%.
With forward EPS of $15.0129, a price of $700 meaning a forward P/E of 47x. Our base case of $347.14 already meaning 23x, so the bold target needs about 24x of additional multiple expansion on today’s earnings.
That multiple looks extreme until you add four years of earnings growth. If EPS rises, the forward P/E contracts fast. FY27 non-GAAP EPS guidance already stands at $16.67 to $16.71. Management is targeting $63 billion in FY30 revenue, up from $41.5 billion in FY26.
The buyback cut reduced shares to 821M from 962M. At $25 of EPS, $700 works out to a more reasonable 28x. A 1.195 adjustment factor, driven by a 1.15 tech sector multiplier and analyst optimism, supports a premium. Our 2030 base and bull cases sit at $634.17 and $670.19.
On the August call, CEO Marc Benioff said, “We’re going from the dumb software era to the smart software era in real time.” Combined Agentforce and Data 360 ARR is nearly $3.9 billion, up more than 210%.
A key risk is that AI agents shrink seat counts faster than consumption pricing can make up the lost revenue.
Where Salesforce Trades Today vs Its Earnings Power
At $246.11, Salesforce trades at 16x forward earnings. That looks cheap for a business guiding to 11% to 12% revenue growth with a 34.3% non-GAAP operating margin.
Shares are trading between a 52-week low of $146.06 and a high of $267.80. The 10-year return is 237.81%. A multiple in the mid-teens leaves the bull case plenty of room to run.
$700 Is a Stretch, but Here’s Why It’s Possible
Hitting $700 requires a 184.4% gain. It’s a stretch, but reachable if three things happen. Agentforce ARR keeps compounding. Premium edition upgrades scale from just 5% of sales and service workers today.
And the $63 billion FY30 target arrives with wider margins. A stall in AI monetization would disrupt it. Such gains shouldn’t be expected every year, but we’ve outlined the plan for how Salesforce could reach $700 in 2030.

Salesforce just agreed to spend billions in cash on a customer engagement platform, and the market is not applauding. Find out why rivals are rising while Salesforce takes the hit and whether the strategic bet on Marketing Cloud justifies the…
Published October 20, 2026, 9:37am ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
© Noam Galai / Getty Images Entertainment via Getty Images
A large all-cash acquisition is weighing on one of the biggest names in enterprise software. Salesforce (NYSE:CRM | CRM Price Prediction) stock is down 2% to $238.57 in morning trading after the company agreed to buy a customer engagement platform.
Braze (NASDAQ:BRZE) is the Salesforce target, a company that helps consumer brands send personalized messages across channels in real time. Under the terms Salesforce announced, the agreement carries an enterprise value of $5.66 billion, with the full amount payable in cash. Approval from Braze shareholders and regulators is still required, and Salesforce made no change to its current fiscal-year guidance.
That cash spending is the core of the trade-off for Salesforce, set against the boost Braze could give Marketing Cloud, while rival software stocks are mostly holding up, which points to a selloff aimed at Salesforce stock.
Braze Deal Targets Marketing Cloud Personalization
Salesforce expects Braze to strengthen cross-channel personalization inside Marketing Cloud. The company also sees the platform complementing its data and Agentforce products, which anchor its push to build AI agents into every part of its software. Marketing Cloud is the piece of Salesforce’s lineup that stands to change most directly.
Patrick Stokes, Salesforce’s president of applications and marketing, stated that Braze was built to turn live customer behavior into personalized engagement at scale. That description lines up with Salesforce’s customer relationship management software, which gains real-time messaging tools built for consumer brands through the deal.
Braze runs its own BrazeAI suite for AI-powered decisioning and customer journey orchestration. Its technology partnerships with AWS, Snowflake and Databricks could give Salesforce more ways to connect with the data systems its customers already use. Those links matter because Salesforce has framed data as the foundation for its AI products.
Customers on the Braze platform span media and entertainment, financial services, retail and technology. This consumer-facing mix gives Salesforce a deeper foothold with brands that need to reach shoppers and subscribers the moment they engage.
Funding a deal of this scale entirely in cash ties up resources Salesforce could otherwise direct elsewhere, and folding a separate platform into Marketing Cloud adds execution risk that typically extends well past closing.
Supporters of the deal can point to the strategic fit for Salesforce. Braze gives Marketing Cloud a purpose-built engine for real-time engagement, and the same guidance means the purchase doesn’t alter management’s current fiscal-year outlook.
Even as CRM stock slips, ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) stock is up 2% to $148.10. Furthermore, Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE) stock is up 2% to $252.47.
The business overlap with Salesforce differs for Adobe and ServiceNow. Marketing software is where Adobe competes with Salesforce, putting it closest to the territory Braze covers. Workflow automation software is ServiceNow’s business, which sits further from the marketing fight.
For a sector read against Salesforce, the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (CBOE:IGV) is down 0.3% to $105.65. Large-cap tech is a touch softer as well, with a NASDAQ 100 tracking fund down 0.5% to $715.16. A modest dip in the software fund next to the sharper drop in Salesforce stock marks the selloff as specific to the company.
Investors are now watching whether regulators clear the Braze deal on schedule. Braze shareholders must also approve the agreement before it can close, and any delay in either review could keep pressure on Salesforce stock.
Until the deal closes and integration progress is visible, Salesforce stock investors should keep their positions moderate. Steady rival software stocks point to deal-specific risk rather than a sector problem, which supports a conservative approach to adding shares.

Why Is Salesforce (CRM) Down 5.5% Since Last Earnings Report?
A month has gone by since the last earnings report for Salesforce (CRM). Shares have lost about 5.5% in that time frame, underperforming the S&P 500.
But investors have to be wondering, will the recent negative trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Salesforce due for a breakout? Well, first let's take a quick look at its latest earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent catalysts for Salesforce, Inc. before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.
Salesforce Q2 Earnings Beat on Investment Gains, Revenue View Raised
Salesforce reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $5.90 per share, up 102.7% year over year. The bottom line beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 80.43%.
Revenues rose 10.8% year over year to $11.35 billion and topped the consensus mark by 0.25%. Growth reflected momentum in Slack, Agentforce and Informatica. Agentforce and Data 360 ARR reached nearly $3.9 billion, up more than 210% year over year.
CRM's Q2 Revenue Mix Shows Broad-Based Growth
Subscription and support revenues increased 11.7% year over year to $10.82 billion, including a $440 million contribution from Informatica. Professional services and other revenues declined 3.8% to $525 million.
Agentforce Apps generated $7.19 billion in subscription and support revenues, with constant-currency growth of 8%. Data 360, Headless Platform and Other contributed $3.62 billion and grew 20% in constant currency. Regionally, the Americas generated $7.4 billion, Europe $2.76 billion and Asia Pacific $1.17 billion, with constant-currency growth of 10%, 13% and 12%, respectively.
Current remaining performance obligation (cRPO) was $33.5 billion, up 14% year over year in constant currency. Total remaining performance obligation reached $66.3 billion, up 11%.
Salesforce's Agentic AI Usage Accelerates
Agentforce ARR exceeded $1.5 billion, rising more than 240% year over year. Customers completed 3.2 billion Agentic Work Units in the quarter, up 97% sequentially, taking cumulative volume across Agentforce and Slack to 7.0 billion.
Slack posted its fastest quarterly net new annual order value growth since the acquisition, while Slackbot users increased more than 150% quarter over quarter. Bookings from Agentforce One Edition and Agentforce for Apps more than doubled sequentially. Management also noted that first-half net new annual order value growth significantly outpaced annual order value growth.
Data 360 ingested 104 trillion records in the quarter, up 355% year over year. Zero Copy ingestion reached 82 trillion records, up 731%, underscoring the rising usage of the company's data layer alongside its agentic products.
CRM's Profitability Reflects Investment Gains
Non-GAAP operating income increased 10.3% year over year to $3.87 billion. The non-GAAP operating margin was 34.1%, down 20 basis points, while the GAAP operating margin fell 230 basis points to 20.5%. Non-GAAP cost of revenues rose to 20% of revenues from 19%, while general and administrative expenses declined to 5% from 6%.
Net gains on strategic investments totaled $2.61 billion compared with $6 million a year earlier. These gains contributed $2.53 per share to second-quarter non-GAAP earnings, providing a substantial boost to the quarter's bottom-line performance.
Salesforce's Cash Flow and Capital Return
In the second quarter, operating cash flow jumped 71.5% year over year to $1.27 billion, while free cash flow increased 81.5% to $1.10 billion. In the first half of fiscal 2027, the company generated operating and free cash flows of $7.97 billion and $7.65 billion, respectively. Salesforce ended the second quarter with $8.31 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $3.09 billion in marketable securities.
The company returned $364 million through dividends during the quarter and continued executing its $25 billion accelerated share repurchase program. Through the first half of fiscal 2027, capital returns totaled $27.9 billion. The share count was down 141 million shares, or 15%, year over year.
Salesforce raised its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $46.10-$46.40 billion from $45.90-$46.20 billion. The $200 million increase, or $300 million in constant currency, reflects $100 million of organic growth and $200 million tied to the pending Contentful and Fin acquisitions, partly offset by a $100 million foreign-exchange headwind. Non-GAAP operating margin guidance remains at 34.3%.
Salesforce lifted its fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings outlook to $16.67-$16.71 per share from $14.06-$14.12. It continues to expect operating cash flow and free cash flow growth of approximately 4%-5% year over year. Updated guidance incorporates the anticipated contributions from Contentful and Fin and is conditional upon the transactions closing.
For the third quarter of fiscal 2027, CRM expects revenues of $11.42-$11.50 billion, implying 11%-12% year-over-year growth, and non-GAAP earnings of $3.42-$3.44 per share. The company expects cRPO growth of approximately 14% year over year and in constant currency.
How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?
Since the earnings release, investors have witnessed a upward trend in estimates revision.
Currently, Salesforce has a nice Growth Score of B, though it is lagging a bit on the Momentum Score front with a C. Charting a somewhat similar path, the stock has a grade of B on the value side, putting it in the second quintile for this investment strategy.
Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of B. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.
Estimates have been broadly trending upward for the stock, and the magnitude of these revisions looks promising. Notably, Salesforce has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). We expect an in-line return from the stock in the next few months.

Salesforce Strikes $5.66 Billion Deal to Buy Customer Engagement Platform Braze
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 9:51 AM CDT 2 min read
Salesforce (CRM) agreed to acquire customer engagement platform Braze (BRZE) in a deal worth $5.66 billion, as it looks to strengthen its business-to-consumer marketing solutions.
Shareholders of Braze's class A stock will receive $47.50 in cash per share, the companies said in a joint Tuesday statement.
Shares of Salesforce fell 0.8% in Tuesday trade, while Braze surged 51%. Salesforce is down 9.3% this year, while Braze is up 32%.
Salesforce expects Braze's real-time engagement and AI capabilities to complement its existing platforms, including Customer 360 and Agentforce. The customer relationship management platform expects the deal to advance its strategy for a more "complete" Customer 360 and strengthen the marketing cloud's cross-channel personalization.
Customer 360 is a suite of unified applications that connects customer data across sales, service, marketing, commerce, IT and operations into a single platform. Agentforce is Salesforce's AI-powered agent platform.
"Braze was built to turn live customer behavior into personalized engagement at scale," Salesforce's president of applications and marketing, Patrick Stokes, said in a statement. "Bringing that capability together with Salesforce marketing cloud, CRM, and Data 360 will deliver that wow moment in every customer interaction."
Salesforce has established a credible AI strategy that reduces the risk of the company becoming obsolete amid a transition toward agentic AI, BofA Securities said Monday.
The deal, which requires approval from Braze's shareholders and clearance from regulators, is expected to complete in Salesforce's fiscal 2028. Salesforce said it doesn't expect the transaction to impact its 2027 guidance.
"Salesforce's platform will help us innovate faster and together we'll help marketers around the world build deeper, more lasting relationships with their customers," Braze Chief Executive Bill Magnuson.
The company has about 2,770 customers, including Canva (CVNA), Instacart (CART), Urban Outfitters (URBN) and PayPal (PYPL) subsidiary Venmo.
Last month, Braze said it expected adjusted earnings between $0.64 and $0.65 per share on a revenue range of $910 million to $913 million for fiscal 2027. In August, Salesforce lifted its full-year revenue outlook after delivering a fiscal second-quarter beat.
In June, Salesforce agreed to acquire customer-agent company Fin for $3.6 billion. Last year, the company completed the purchase of Informatica for about $8 billion.
In the broader industry, ServiceNow (NOW) completed its acquisition of Armis in April for roughly $7.75 billion. SAP (SAP) acquired Prior Labs in July. Late last year, Workday (WDAY) bought AI company Sana for about $1.1 billion.

BRZE stock surged more than 50%, hitting a 20-month high, even as Piper Sandler, Wells Fargo, Loop Capital and Stifel lowered their ratings following the announcement.

Analysts See Shareholder Win, Broader Software Implications
In a note to investors cited by TheFly, Wells Fargo downgraded Braze to 'Equal Weight' from 'Overweight', but raised the price target to $47.50 from $45. According to The Fly, the brokerage said Braze investors would likely welcome the acquisition.
The firm viewed increased deal activity as positive for the broader software sector, potentially helping investors address questions about long-term valuations.
Stifel downgraded Braze to 'Hold' from 'Buy', while lifting its price target to $47.50 from $35. The firm described the approximately 58% acquisition premium as "a win for Braze shareholders," noting that the offer values the stock at its highest level since March 2024.
Piper Sandler analyst Billy Fitzsimmons also downgraded Braze to 'Neutral' from 'Overweight' following the acquisition agreement, per TheFly. Loop Capital analyst Yun Kim also downgraded Braze to 'Hold' from 'Buy', raising the price target to $47.50 from $40.
Meanwhile, Jefferies said the acquisition could "re-energize" Salesforce's Marketing and Commerce Cloud business and strengthen its competitiveness against Adobe (ADBE). The firm maintained a 'Buy' rating and $300 price target on Salesforce.
Evercore Flags Salesforce Deal Price, M&A Pace
Evercore ISI said the rationale behind Salesforce's acquisition of Braze makes sense, given the latter's fast-growing consumer engagement business, but warned that the timing and price were "likely to be a bit of a debate," according to The Fly.
The firm noted that the $47.50 per share offer represents a roughly 58% premium to Braze's previous closing price of $30.04, and approximately 80% above its 30-day average share price.
However, Evercore also warned that Salesforce's recent pace of acquisitions could concern value-focused investors, while identifying ServiceNow (NOW) as a potential beneficiary of investor fund flows. The firm maintained an 'Outperform' rating and $290 price target on Salesforce.
Braze's Growth Drew Analyst Support Before Deal
Before the acquisition announcement, several analysts had maintained positive ratings on Braze following its quarterly results and annual Forge conference.
Braze's U.S. revenue rose 27.2% year over year to $125.6 million in its fiscal second quarter (Q2), while international revenue increased 24.9% to $101.7 million, according to its Form 10-Q.
Following Forge, DA Davidson maintained a 'Buy' rating and $40 price target, citing customer and partner feedback about replacing incumbent marketing platforms, According to Investing.com, Cantor Fitzgerald reiterated 'Overweight' with a $38 target,
Citizens maintained 'Market Outperform' with a $35 target, pointing to encouraging customer spending plans. Raymond James had also maintained an 'Outperform' rating with a $33 target following Braze's September earnings report.
The transaction is expected to close in Salesforce's fiscal 2028, subject to Braze shareholder approval and regulatory clearances. Salesforce (CRM) said it does not anticipate changes to its fiscal 2027 guidance and has not updated its long-term financial targets in connection with the acquisition.

The subject of this case is Salesforce's all-cash acquisition of Braze, which possesses a customer engagement platform (a mechanism for managing notifications and messages delivered to customers), for an enterprise value of approximately $5.66 billion, and whether it can incorporate customer touchpoints in the AI era into its own product layer.

A large all-cash acquisition is weighing on one of the biggest names in enterprise software. Salesforce (NYSE:CRM | CRM Price Prediction) stock is down 2% to $238.57 in morning trading after the company agreed to buy a customer engagement platform.
Braze (NASDAQ:BRZE) is the Salesforce target, a company that helps consumer brands send personalized messages across channels in real time. Under the terms Salesforce announced, the agreement carries an enterprise value of $5.66 billion, with the full amount payable in cash. Approval from Braze shareholders and regulators is still required, and Salesforce made no change to its current fiscal-year guidance.
That cash spending is the core of the trade-off for Salesforce, set against the boost Braze could give Marketing Cloud, while rival software stocks are mostly holding up, which points to a selloff aimed at Salesforce stock.
Braze Deal Targets Marketing Cloud Personalization
Salesforce expects Braze to strengthen cross-channel personalization inside Marketing Cloud. The company also sees the platform complementing its data and Agentforce products, which anchor its push to build AI agents into every part of its software. Marketing Cloud is the piece of Salesforce’s lineup that stands to change most directly.
Patrick Stokes, Salesforce’s president of applications and marketing, stated that Braze was built to turn live customer behavior into personalized engagement at scale. That description lines up with Salesforce’s customer relationship management software, which gains real-time messaging tools built for consumer brands through the deal.
Braze runs its own BrazeAI suite for AI-powered decisioning and customer journey orchestration. Its technology partnerships with AWS, Snowflake and Databricks could give Salesforce more ways to connect with the data systems its customers already use. Those links matter because Salesforce has framed data as the foundation for its AI products.
Customers on the Braze platform span media and entertainment, financial services, retail and technology. This consumer-facing mix gives Salesforce a deeper foothold with brands that need to reach shoppers and subscribers the moment they engage.
Funding a deal of this scale entirely in cash ties up resources Salesforce could otherwise direct elsewhere, and folding a separate platform into Marketing Cloud adds execution risk that typically extends well past closing.
Supporters of the deal can point to the strategic fit for Salesforce. Braze gives Marketing Cloud a purpose-built engine for real-time engagement, and the same guidance means the purchase doesn’t alter management’s current fiscal-year outlook.
Even as CRM stock slips, ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) stock is up 2% to $148.10. Furthermore, Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE) stock is up 2% to $252.47.
The business overlap with Salesforce differs for Adobe and ServiceNow. Marketing software is where Adobe competes with Salesforce, putting it closest to the territory Braze covers. Workflow automation software is ServiceNow’s business, which sits further from the marketing fight.
For a sector read against Salesforce, the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (CBOE:IGV) is down 0.3% to $105.65. Large-cap tech is a touch softer as well, with a NASDAQ 100 tracking fund down 0.5% to $715.16. A modest dip in the software fund next to the sharper drop in Salesforce stock marks the selloff as specific to the company.
Investors are now watching whether regulators clear the Braze deal on schedule. Braze shareholders must also approve the agreement before it can close, and any delay in either review could keep pressure on Salesforce stock.
Until the deal closes and integration progress is visible, Salesforce stock investors should keep their positions moderate. Steady rival software stocks point to deal-specific risk rather than a sector problem, which supports a conservative approach to adding shares.

Salesforce Signs Definitive Agreement to Acquire Braze
SAN FRANCISCO & NEW YORK (OCTOBER 20, 2026) — Salesforce (NYSE: CRM), the world’s #1 AI CRM, today announced it has
entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Braze (NASDAQ: BRZE), a leading customer engagement platform, for approximately $5.66 billion in enterprise value. Under the terms of the agreement, holders of Braze Class A common stock will
receive $47.50 in cash per share.
Braze helps marketers build deeper customer relationships by responding to customer behavior in real time, coordinating
personalized experiences across mobile apps, websites, email, SMS, WhatsApp, and more. Its cloud-native, event-streaming architecture is optimized for high-volume, real-time B2C engagement, continuously updating customer profiles and adapting
customer journeys while powering trillions of messages and journey actions each year. BrazeAI extends these capabilities with AI-powered optimization across content, offers, channels, and timing, helping
marketers make each interaction more relevant.
“Every interaction is an opportunity to wow your customers,” said Patrick Stokes, President,
Applications and Marketing, Salesforce. “Most of that wow comes from knowing your customer, and responding at just the right moment. Braze was built to turn live customer behavior into personalized engagement at scale. Bringing that capability
together with Salesforce Marketing Cloud, CRM, and Data 360 will deliver that wow moment in every customer interaction.”
the conviction that marketers and their creativity are a brand’s ultimate competitive advantage,” said Bill Magnuson, CEO and Co-Founder of Braze. “This past year we shipped at the fastest
pace in our history, and BrazeAI is helping marketers get their best ideas live faster. Salesforce shares our commitment to marketers, and we’ll continue building as Braze and investing in the Braze community of customers and partners who
built this company with us. Salesforce’s platform will help us innovate faster and together we’ll help marketers around the world build deeper, more lasting relationships with their customers.”
AI is raising the bar for marketers, who now need agentic solutions that can understand customers, make decisions, and act in real time. Salesforce is moving
to lead that shift, through both organic innovation and acquisitions that meet the standards of our M&A framework: advancing customer success, fitting within our strategy, accelerating innovation, and creating long-term value.
Following the close of the transaction, Braze’s real-time engagement and AI decisioning capabilities are expected to complement all four layers of
Salesforce’s architecture — Data 360, Customer 360, Agentforce, and SIForce. Within Customer 360, Braze is expected to strengthen Marketing Cloud’s cross-channel personalization, helping brands turn a deeper view of each customer
into richer experiences, optimized in real time at the scale needed to reach hundreds of millions of people.
Salesforce’s vision for a more complete Customer 360 and expand how brands connect with customers across high-volume B2C experiences. Salesforce and Braze also share a commitment to an open, composable approach that gives customers flexibility
across the data, tools, and partners they rely on.
Together, Salesforce and Braze would help businesses:
Act on customer behavior in real time. Braze’s event-streaming architecture turns live customer
signals and data from cloud data warehouses and other platforms into personalized messages and coordinated journeys, helping marketers adapt engagement as customers browse, buy, and use products.
Deliver richer experiences across channels. Braze’s deep mobile and app capabilities, including in-app messages, personalized content feeds, and live updates, work alongside email, web, and messaging channels to create more connected customer experiences.
Make personalization more intelligent. Braze’s AI decisioning helps marketers optimize content,
offers, channels, and timing. Bringing these capabilities together with Salesforce’s customer context and Agentforce would help businesses make engagement more relevant and connect marketing with the broader customer relationship across
commerce, sales, and service.
Braze serves approximately 2,770 customers, including Canva, Dairy Queen, Equinox, Instacart, Urban
Outfitters, and Venmo. Led by co-founders Bill Magnuson and Jon Hyman, Braze would also bring deep expertise in mobile experiences, data engineering, and customer engagement to Salesforce Marketing Cloud.
in Salesforce’s fiscal year 2028, subject to customary closing conditions, including approval by Braze’s shareholders and receipt of required regulatory approvals. There is no anticipated change to Salesforce’s FY27 guidance.
Salesforce has not guided FY28 and there is no update to long-term targets at this time.
J.P. Morgan Securities LLC is serving as exclusive financial advisor to Salesforce, and Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz and Covington &
Burling LLP are serving as legal counsel to Salesforce.
Qatalyst Partners is serving as exclusive financial advisor to Braze, and Davis Polk &
Wardwell LLP is serving as legal counsel to Braze.
